signals.entity: Migration Department (Τμήμα Μετανάστευσης), Cyprus / JCC Payment Systems Ltd
signals.signal: OPEN/under evaluation tender ΤΜ/1/2026/ΑΔ: 'Παροχή υπηρεσιών για εγκατάσταση και λειτουργία αυτόματης ταμειακής μηχανής στον διεθνή αερολιμένα Γλαύκου Κληρίδη στη Λάρνακα' - services for the installation and operation of an ATM at Larnaca Glafkos Clerides International Airport for the Assisted Voluntary Returns Programme. CPV 66100000 (banking and investment services), Law 73(I)/2016, open procedure, lowest price, estimated value EUR 47,712. Published 11/06/2026; bids due 30/06/2026 12:00; opened 30/06/2026 12:30. Exactly ONE bid was opened: JCC Payment Systems Ltd, EUR 43,200.00. Status on e-PPS as at 01/08/2026: Αξιολόγηση (under evaluation). Specification is an ATM-as-a-service contract: installation within one week of signature; the contractor bears all connectivity (cable/telephone/network) and its cost; 24/7 operation; the machine must dispense EUR 50, EUR 100 and EUR 200 notes at the user's choice, hold a cash stock of at least EUR 200,000, and permit withdrawals of up to EUR 20,000 per transaction; the contractor must replenish within 24 hours whenever the stock falls below EUR 150,000.
signals.source_name: eprocurement.gov.cy (e-PPS) - tender overview and bid-opening detail, ΤΜ/1/2026/ΑΔ
signals.implies: This is the off-site ATM-placement-and-operation model Printec already owns in Greece through Printec Cash Network / Cashflex - a government body buying a deployed, cash-loaded, 24/7-operated ATM as a priced service rather than buying hardware. It proves the contracting shape is available in Cyprus under CPV 66100000. It also shows only one operator (JCC Payment Systems) currently answers such calls, so the segment is uncontested and priced accordingly (EUR 43.2k against a EUR 47.7k estimate, i.e. a 9% discount only).
signals.likelihood: Award imminent (evaluation open since 30/06/2026); further government/airport/port ATM-siting calls plausible within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Register Printec (or Printec Cash Network) as an economic operator on e-PPS immediately and set alerts on CPV 66100000 and 'αυτόματη ταμειακή μηχανή'; build a Cyprus ATM-as-a-service proposition benchmarked at the EUR 43.2k / EUR 200k-cash-stock spec; assess whether to compete with or partner JCC.

signals.entity: Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation & Digital Policy (Υφυπουργείο Έρευνας, Καινοτομίας και Ψηφιακής Πολιτικής) / JCC Payment Systems Ltd
signals.signal: Tender ΥΕΚΨΠ/2024/13/Δ/Δ 'ΔΙΑΓΩΝΙΣΜΟΣ ΓΙΑ ΑΓΟΡΑ ΗΛΕΚΤΡΟΝΙΚΩΝ ΤΑΥΤΟΤΗΤΩΝ ΓΙΑ ΧΡΗΣΗ ΑΠΟ ΤΟΥΣ ΠΟΛΙΤΕΣ ΤΗΣ ΔΗΜΟΚΡΑΤΙΑΣ ΑΝΩ ΤΩΝ 18 ΕΤΩΝ' (purchase of electronic identities for citizens of the Republic aged over 18) ran as a negotiated procedure WITHOUT prior publication over two cycles: cycle 1 published 23/10/2024, closing 29/10/2024; cycle 2 closing 27/02/2025. In BOTH cycles the only economic operator recorded on the e-PPS bid-opening page was JCC Payment Systems Ltd (offers 7142996 and 7375166, lodged 'Εκτός συστήματος' / off-system, so no price is disclosed). Status on e-PPS as at 01/08/2026: Ανατεθειμένο (awarded); award date 04/04/2025.
signals.implies: The Cypriot national card processor/acquirer JCC Payment Systems - owned by the Cypriot banks - has been sole-sourced the citizen-facing electronic-identity credential. That puts the payments switch, not a security vendor, at the centre of Cyprus' digital-identity stack, and pairs with the Veridos eMRTD prime contract as the two halves of the national ID programme. For Printec, JCC is the decisive channel partner (or blocker) for digital onboarding/eKYC, credential verification hardware and HSM work in Cyprus - and, per the Larnaca airport ATM tender, the same company is the incumbent in ATM-as-a-service.
signals.likelihood: eID rollout to adults continues through 2026-2027; eKYC and credential-verification integration demand follows
signals.followup: Open a partner conversation with JCC Payment Systems Ltd (Nicosia) covering eID-based onboarding/eKYC, verification hardware and HSM; request the contract value from the Deputy Ministry, since the e-PPS record carries no price.

signals.entity: Migration Department / Ministry of Interior (Cyprus) - Veridos GmbH
signals.signal: Award published 29/07/2026 on TED for an 'end-to-end solution for the issuance of eMRTDs' (ref 1/2023/TAPM/KD) - enrolment system, personalisation system, PKI, SPOC and inspection/verification system, plus eMRTD document supply. Estimated value EUR 34,550,000 excl. VAT; awarded value EUR 22,900,450 excl. VAT to Veridos GmbH (Berlin, reg. 21996). Four tenders received; contract concluded 18/12/2024; restricted procedure, lowest price. CPVs 22450000/22451000/22455000 (security-type printed matter).
signals.implies: Confirms Veridos (Giesecke+Devrient group) as prime on Cyprus' national biometric-document programme, including the PKI/HSM and enrolment/verification layers - the same G+D group already logged as an incumbent at NBS Serbia and Banka Slovenije. For Printec this is competitor lock-in on the state identity stack, but the EUR 11.6m gap between estimate and award, plus downstream enrolment desks, verification terminals and PKI/HSM maintenance, is addressable through Printec's digital onboarding/eKYC and HSM/security lines and via a subcontract/partner route.
signals.likelihood: Adjacent work packages (enrolment kiosks, verification terminals, PKI/HSM support) likely to surface as separate notices within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Watch eprocurement.gov.cy and TED for Migration Department / Civil Registry follow-on lots; map Veridos' Cyprus subcontracting and cross-reference with the G+D relationships already logged in Serbia and Slovenia.

signals.entity: Electricity Authority of Cyprus (Αρχή Ηλεκτρισμού Κύπρου, EAC)
signals.signal: Tender 202/2025 'Προμήθεια, Εγκατάσταση και Συντήρηση Μηχανών Καταμέτρησης Χαρτονομισμάτων' (supply, installation and maintenance of banknote-counting machines). Utilities regime (Law 140(I)/2016 / Dir. 2014/25/EU), open procedure, lowest price, CPV 30100000, estimated value EUR 55,000, published 26/08/2025, bids due 08/10/2025, opened 09/10/2025. Four bids were opened: TH.K. Office Supplies Ltd EUR 31,400.00; MASTERTYPE C.P. Services Ltd EUR 33,000.00; A. Finiris Co Ltd EUR 43,600.00; Brink's Cyprus (Private Security Services) Limited EUR 59,050.00. Status on e-PPS as at 01/08/2026 is still 'Αξιολόγηση' (under evaluation) - no award almost ten months after opening.
signals.implies: The only genuine cash-automation procurement visible in the Cypriot public sector, mapping directly to Printec's cash automation / banknote counting and authentication line. It also exposes the Cyprus competitive set for counting equipment: two office-equipment dealers (TH.K. Office Supplies, MASTERTYPE C.P. Services), A. Finiris Co, and - notably - the CIT operator Brink's Cyprus bidding equipment rather than services. Printec did not bid. Small ticket, but it is the reference beachhead for Cypriot cash handling and mirrors the Greek pattern where resellers (Ταμειακή Εξπρές, BOOS) hold the counting-machine channel.
signals.likelihood: Award or cancellation/re-tender likely within 6 months given the stalled evaluation
signals.followup: Register on e-PPS and alert on EAC utilities notices; if 202/2025 is cancelled, bid the relaunch. Profile TH.K. Office Supplies Ltd and MASTERTYPE C.P. Services Ltd as the local counting-equipment channel and assess Brink's Cyprus as a partner rather than a rival.

signals.entity: Εθνική Αρχή Στοιχημάτων (Cyprus National Betting Authority) / Logicom Solutions Ltd
signals.signal: Award notice Α.Α.98.2026 'SIEM - SOC', published on TED 12/06/2026. Direct award (negotiated without prior call for competition) of the 'Hawk 360' managed security service - centralised event monitoring and analysis, 24x7 detection and response by a dedicated security team, delivered without additional on-premise servers - to Logicom Solutions Ltd (Nicosia, reg. 1626, SME) for EUR 87,750 excl. VAT. Only one tender received. Stated justification: absence of competition for technical reasons, because the incumbent built the Authority's existing infrastructure and switching would re-incur installation and interconnection costs.
signals.implies: Identifies Logicom Solutions Ltd (Logicom Group) as the Cypriot managed-SOC/SIEM incumbent, and shows the Cypriot renewal pattern: security monitoring is re-awarded directly to whoever installed it. That is the competitive reality Printec's managed-services/SOC line faces around the Central Bank of Cyprus SIEM tender 02/2026 and any bank-side monitoring deal - first install wins the annuity, so Printec must target greenfield rather than renewals.
signals.likelihood: Renewal cycle recurs annually; comparable direct awards likely at other Cypriot public bodies
signals.followup: Profile Logicom Solutions Ltd as the primary Cyprus security-services competitor/partner; target greenfield SIEM/SOC installs and new-build entities instead of incumbent renewals.

signals.signal: CBC Tender 08/2026 OPEN: purchase of services supporting on-site AML inspections at CBC-supervised institutions under the 2007 AML Law and its directives, for three (3) years. Estimated value EUR 900,000 excl. VAT. Open procedure, lowest price. The contract is split into lots by category of supervised institution and CBC will award to UP TO FOUR contractors ranked by offer. Documents available 03/07/2026-07/08/2026; bids due 07/08/2026 12:00 Cyprus time at CBC Office 018, 80 J. Kennedy Ave, Nicosia. A revised financial-offer table and a Q&A file have been posted. Also carried on TED as notice 460289-2026 (03/07/2026, CPV 79210000).
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Cyprus - Προσφορές, Διαγωνισμός 08/2026 (also TED 460289-2026)
signals.implies: Direct evidence of CBC scaling its AML supervisory capacity with outside capacity. Printec's AML/compliance and transaction-monitoring line is adjacent: inspection findings drive remediation spend at the supervised banks, EMIs and PSPs, which is Printec's actual buying centre. The four-contractor structure also lowers the barrier for a consortium entry.
signals.likelihood: Award expected Q4 2026; downstream AML-remediation demand at Cypriot banks/EMIs high
signals.followup: Track the award/winners after 07/08/2026 and use the four appointed inspection firms as channel partners into Cypriot banks and EMIs for AML and transaction-monitoring tooling.

signals.signal: CBC Tender 02/2026 for maintenance/system management and 24-hour Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) services for three years, estimated EUR 370,000 excl. VAT, open procedure, lowest price. Deadlines were extended: clarification deadlines to 02/04/2026 and 09/04/2026, and bid submission moved from 17/04/2026 to 24/04/2026 12:00. As at 01/08/2026 no award notice for 02/2026 appears on the CBC tenders or announcements pages; no corresponding contract-award notice appears in the 377-notice TED Cyprus set for 01/06/2026-01/08/2026; and 02/2026 is no longer listed among CBC's open tenders (only 08/2026, 12/2026 and 15/2026 are). CBC does not publish through e-PPS at all - a search of the e-PPS opened-tender register by contracting authority 'ΚΕΝΤΡΙΚΗ ΤΡΑΠΕΖΑ' returns zero records - so the CBC website plus TED are the only disclosure channels.
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Cyprus announcement - Διαγωνισμός 02/2026 (SIEM)
signals.implies: CBC is buying an outsourced 24x7 security-monitoring service - the same managed-security envelope Printec sells as managed services alongside HSM/security. An unannounced outcome more than three months after closing suggests either a quiet award or a failed/relaunched procedure; either way it is a re-entry point. The Betting Authority precedent (Logicom Solutions, direct award on incumbency) shows how these consolidate in Cyprus, so a relaunch is the realistic window.
signals.likelihood: Award or re-tender disclosure within 6 months
signals.followup: Ask CBC (cbctenders@centralbank.cy) or check the Official Gazette for the 02/2026 outcome; if cancelled, position Printec managed SOC/SIEM for the relaunch. Do not expect this on e-PPS.

signals.signal: CBC Tender 04/2026: purchase of installation, configuration, support and maintenance services for ORACLE software to upgrade the availability of CBC's databases. Estimated value EUR 260,000 excl. VAT, open procedure, lowest price; documents 06/02/2026-20/03/2026, bids due 20/03/2026 12:00. No award published on CBC's site as at 01/08/2026 and none found on TED.
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Cyprus announcement - Διαγωνισμός 04/2026 (ORACLE)
signals.implies: Shows CBC's 2026 IT budget going into resilience/high-availability infrastructure - the platform layer under any payment, settlement or supervisory system. Relevant to Printec managed services and useful for mapping which local system integrators hold CBC's infrastructure accounts.
signals.followup: Identify the 04/2026 winner to map CBC's incumbent infrastructure integrator in Cyprus.

signals.signal: CBC Tender 12/2026 OPEN: contract for the minting, packaging and delivery of Cypriot euro silver and gold collector coins. Open procedure, award on lowest price, CPV 18512100 (coins). Tender documents available from 10/07/2026; bids due 04/09/2026. Published on TED as notice 477731-2026 (10/07/2026). A CBC answers-to-questions document was posted 30/07/2026, indicating live bidder interest.
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Cyprus - Tender No. 12/2026 (also TED 477731-2026)
signals.implies: Not a Printec product line (minting is a mint-house business), but it confirms CBC still runs its own cash and coin supply chain in house and procures around it - the cash-cycle context in which coin/banknote handling, counting and authentication equipment (Printec cash automation) is bought. Log as market structure, not a bid.
signals.followup: Watch for a companion CBC notice on coin/banknote handling, counting or authentication equipment, which would be a genuine Printec cash-automation opening.

signals.entity: Department of Postal Services (Τμήμα Ταχυδρομικών Υπηρεσιών / Cyprus Post)
signals.signal: Cyprus Post's own public tender page (cypruspost.post/el/prosfores) has not been updated since 2024 - its last listed notices are ΤΥΣΔ 25/24 (18/12/2024) and earlier; there is no 2025 or 2026 section. Live procurement runs entirely through e-PPS, where the 2025-2026 record for Τμήμα Ταχυδρομικών Υπηρεσιών contains only logistics, guarding and back-office IT: T.Y. 10/26 inland mail transport (EUR 643,150 est., 24 months + 3, CPV 60160000, published 09/06/2026, bids due 30/06/2026, a single bid from C.S.A. Savva General Works Ltd, still in evaluation); T.Y. 7/26 guarding of the mail sorting centre (closed 22/05/2026); 25.127.ΣΣ.ΗΜΥ maintenance of security systems in post offices Cyprus-wide (awarded 07/11/2025); and ΤΥΠ2026/006/Δ/B, a negotiated award of SAP licence subscription for Cyprus Post's 'ΖΗΝΩΝ' system (awarded 15/06/2026). Keyword sweeps of the full 18,187-record e-PPS opened-tender register for ATM, self-service, κερματ (coin), χρηματοκιβ (safe), HSM, ανακύκλ (recycling) and αυτόματων ταμειακών returned NO Cyprus Post self-service, parcel-locker, cash-automation or payment-terminal notice.
signals.source_name: eprocurement.gov.cy (e-PPS) opened-tender register (keyword 'Ταχυδρομ') and cypruspost.post Προσφορές page
signals.implies: Cyprus Post is NOT currently a self-service or cash-automation buyer, unlike ELTA Greece, Ukrposhta or Slovenska posta. Its only automation spend is a SAP back-office subscription plus physical-security maintenance. For Printec this is a negative qualification: deprioritise Cyprus Post for ATM/kiosk/cash-recycler outreach this cycle and monitor e-PPS - not the Cyprus Post website - if that changes.
signals.likelihood: Low - no self-service programme visible anywhere in the 2026 pipeline
signals.followup: Set an e-PPS alert on contracting authority 'Τμήμα Ταχυδρομικών Υπηρεσιών'; revisit only if a postal-automation or parcel-locker line appears.

signals.signal: OPEN tender CHC/01/2026 'Tender for the provision of Information Security Managed Services', CPV 72220000 + 72800000 + 80000000, estimated value EUR 270,000 excl. VAT, duration 60 months, open procedure under the utilities directive 2014/25/EU, award on best price-quality ratio, English-language submission, electronic submission required, SME-suitable. Clarifications closed 22/07/2026; deadline for receipt of tenders 12/08/2026 17:00 (EEST). Documents at eprocurement.gov.cy resourceId 9096401. Published on TED 09/07/2026.
signals.implies: A five-year managed information-security contract from a state-owned utility that accepts English-language bids and is explicitly SME-suitable - the most accessible Cyprus entry point in this window for Printec's managed-services/security line, with no incumbent-renewal lock-in visible (unlike the Betting Authority direct award).
signals.followup: Assess bidding CHC/01/2026 before 12/08/2026 - English submission removes the local-language barrier and the 60-month term makes it an annuity worth chasing.

signals.signal: OPEN tender TA 03/2024 'Provision, implementation, maintenance and operation of an Integrated System for the Department of Insolvency (DoI) and the provision of Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)'. Estimated value EUR 5,652,000 excl. VAT; CPVs include 72212217 transaction-processing software development, 48800000/48810000 information systems and servers, 48517000 IT software package, 50312000/50312300 maintenance of computer and data-network equipment. Term up to 12 years (up to 2 years implementation, 1 year good-operation guarantee, 4 years support/operation/maintenance plus IaaS, 5 years optional extension). Open procedure; TED notice 414250-2026 published 17/06/2026; deadline for receipt of tenders 15/09/2026.
signals.implies: The largest open Cypriot financial-sector IT procurement in this window, sitting on the debt/insolvency side of the banking market that Printec's compliance and managed-services customers touch. Not core Printec hardware, but a credible consortium/subcontract play on the IaaS and managed-service layers, and a marker of which system integrator wins Cyprus' financial-infrastructure accounts for the next decade.
signals.likelihood: Award H1 2027 given the 15/09/2026 deadline and 12-year term
signals.followup: Identify likely primes (Logicom Solutions, Deloitte Limited, DOTSOFT and other recurring Cyprus winners) and evaluate a subcontract position on the IaaS/managed-service layer.

signals.entity: Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (Επιτροπή Κεφαλαιαγοράς Κύπρου, CySEC)
signals.signal: Tender ΕΚΚ 04/2026 'Παροχή Υπηρεσιών Υποδομής Azure Cloud για το σύστημα EMIR-SFTR Cloud' - provision of Azure cloud infrastructure for CySEC's EMIR-SFTR transaction-reporting system for three years, procured through a Microsoft-authorised Cloud Solution Provider holding Infrastructure (Azure) Microsoft Solution Partner status. Estimated value EUR 250,000 excl. VAT, open procedure, lowest price, Greek-language submission, bids due 20/07/2026 13:00, public opening 20/07/2026 13:30. TED notice 425231-2026 published 22/06/2026.
signals.implies: Cyprus' securities regulator is moving its derivatives and securities-financing transaction-reporting infrastructure to public cloud. Transaction reporting and surveillance sit next to Printec's transaction-monitoring and AML/compliance line, and the regulator's own cloud-first posture is a usable argument that cloud/managed delivery is acceptable for supervised firms in Cyprus.
signals.likelihood: Award Q3-Q4 2026; the regulator's cloud posture is a standing enabler
signals.followup: Cite CySEC's own cloud adoption when pitching cloud/managed AML and transaction-monitoring to Cypriot banks, EMIs and investment firms.

signals.entity: Cyprus public sector - Digital Security Authority (Αρχή Ψηφιακής Ασφάλειας) and the KDP 389/2020 + KDP 245/2024 regime
signals.signal: A standing, decree-driven cybersecurity-compliance market is visible on e-PPS, all citing Regulatory Decree KDP 389/2020 and the cybersecurity maturity model set by KDP 245/2024: Nicosia District Self-Government Organisation 53/2026 (assurance audit against KDP 389/2020 using the KDP 245/2024 maturity model, closed 26/06/2026, in evaluation); Larnaca EOAL 61/2025 and Limassol M7/2025 equivalents (both awarded); Health Insurance Organisation ΟΑΥ 25/2024 information-security review and KDP 389/2020 compliance (awarded 23/01/2026); Cyprus Ports Authority ΠΡ.25/2025 cybersecurity-framework development and support (awarded 24/07/2026); OKYPY K.O. 194/25 security-awareness platform; Cyprus Agricultural Payments Organisation ΟΑΠ/ΥΑΠ/01/25/04 information-security consultancy (awarded 19/08/2025). Separately the Digital Security Authority is building a national SOC under project 'SENTINEL 1': ΑΨΑ 09/2025 six servers for SOC sensors (awarded 18/03/2026) and ΑΨΑ 41/2025 host intrusion-detection systems for the SOC including installation, configuration, training and annual support (awarded 02/03/2026); it also ran ΑΨΑ 81/2025 and ΑΨΑ 83/2025 to contract in cybersecurity engineers and analysts (both awarded 18/05/2026).
signals.implies: Cyprus has a regulation-driven audit and monitoring market with repeat quarterly demand across public bodies and critical-infrastructure operators, and the state's own security authority is both building a national SOC and buying in scarce cyber skills. This is the demand engine Printec's security and managed-services line can attach to, and it is the same regulatory logic that will push supervised banks toward outsourced monitoring - the pull-through for CBC 02/2026 and any bank-side SOC deal.
signals.likelihood: Continuous - new KDP 389/2020 audit notices appear every quarter
signals.followup: Register on e-PPS and monitor CPV 72500000/72220000/79212000 notices citing KDP 389/2020 or KDP 245/2024; package a Printec compliance-audit plus managed-monitoring offer for Cypriot public bodies and banks; explore supplying the Digital Security Authority's SENTINEL programme.

signals.entity: Cyprus banking sector (Association of Cyprus Banks members)
signals.signal: Association of Cyprus Banks data compiled by InBusinessNews and published 02/07/2026 gives the current Cypriot ATM estate: 321 ATMs across 8 member banks in 2026, against 423 across 12 members in 2013. Per bank in 2026: Eurobank 156 ATMs / 59 branches / 2,450 staff; Bank of Cyprus 132 ATMs / 56 branches / 2,447 staff; Alpha Bank Cyprus 26 ATMs / 25 branches; National Bank of Greece (Cyprus) 4 ATMs / 2 branches; Societe Generale Bank Cyprus 3 ATMs / 3 branches; Ancoria Bank, cdbbank and Housing Finance Corporation operate 0 ATMs. Total branches fell from 384 to 155 and staff from 9,273 to 6,253 over the period.
signals.source_name: CBN Cyprus (InBusinessNews) - 'A look at Cyprus's evolving banking landscape: The employees, branches and ATMs in numbers', citing Association of Cyprus Banks annual reports
signals.implies: Hard sizing for Printec's Cyprus ATM/self-service opportunity: a 321-unit addressable fleet concentrated in just two banks (Eurobank 156 + Bank of Cyprus 132 = 90% of the market). ATM count fell only 24% while branches fell 60%, so self-service is absorbing the branch retreat - the classic trigger for deposit/recycling upgrades. Two banks means two deals decide the market; there is no public-tender route into either, so this is a direct-sales beat, not a portal beat.
signals.likelihood: Fleet refresh decisions driven by the Eurobank integration and BoC's branch-model rollout over 2026-2027
signals.followup: Build named account plans for Eurobank Limited (Cyprus) and Bank of Cyprus; these are private buyers, so approach through direct sales and JCC, not through eprocurement.gov.cy.

signals.signal: Bank of Cyprus' published branch model (implemented from January 2025) is a four-tier network: 29 full-service Branches, 12 Lending Units, 15 Transaction Branches and 5 unmanned Digital Branches, plus 17 extended-hours self-service points across all districts operating until 22:00 with card-activated controlled access. The machines documented at those points are: ATMs (deposits, withdrawals, transfers, balance, statement printing); Business Deposit Machines for banknote and coin deposits via security envelopes; Coin Deposit/Withdrawal Machines with automatic counting and deposit-slip issuance; and Digital Branch equipment described as '360 Notes' and '360 Coins' systems for business deposits using security codes. Four branches (Nicosia, Limassol, Larnaca, Paphos) have been renovated with dedicated self-service areas.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus - New Branch Model (official site)
signals.implies: Bank of Cyprus has already committed to an unmanned/self-service operating model with deposit automation, coin handling and business cash deposit - exactly Printec's cash automation, recycler and self-service portfolio - and is running dedicated 'Digital Branch' formats that need continuing hardware, servicing and managed-services supply. The named '360 Notes' / '360 Coins' units (Hellenic Bank's equivalent was branded 'Cash 360') indicate an installed base of third-party cash-deposit machines whose service and refresh cycle is contestable.
signals.likelihood: Digital-branch expansion continuing; hardware refresh and managed-service renewal decisions within 12-24 months
signals.followup: Establish the OEM behind the '360 Notes'/'360 Coins' units at Bank of Cyprus and the service incumbent; position Printec recyclers, coin handling and managed services against the 5 digital branches and 17 extended-hours points.

signals.signal: Hellenic Bank was merged into Eurobank Cyprus on 01/09/2025, retiring the Hellenic Bank brand and creating Eurobank Limited. As reported 15/09/2025, fifteen branches were then operating under a branch-in-branch model (eight ex-Eurobank, seven ex-Hellenic) pending full network integration, and the rebranding required updating documents, websites and ATMs. Deputy CEO Hambakis stated that significant investment in branch renovations and digital platforms was planned over the following two years. Hellenic Bank had previously launched dedicated automated service points in Nicosia, Limassol, Larnaca and Paphos with real-time cash withdrawal and deposit, cheque deposit, balance, transfers, and 'Cash 360' machines for larger cash and coin deposits by personal and business customers after registration. Per the Association of Cyprus Banks 2026 figures the merged bank now runs 156 ATMs and 59 branches, the largest estate in Cyprus.
signals.source_name: Cyprus Mail - 'Eurobank hails seamless merger, outlines next steps for clients'; Cyprus Mail - 'Hellenic Bank launches new automated service points'
signals.implies: A merged bank running two inherited self-service estates, publicly committed to two years of branch and digital investment, and now the largest ATM operator in Cyprus at 156 units. Fleet rationalisation after a merger is the single highest-probability trigger for ATM/recycler replacement, cash-management consolidation and a managed-services contract - and Printec has the directly comparable Greek reference in Eurobank's home market. Highest-value non-tender target in Cyprus.
signals.likelihood: Integration and estate rationalisation decisions run through 2026-2027
signals.followup: Prioritise a direct approach to Eurobank Limited (Cyprus) on ATM/recycler fleet rationalisation, cash-cycle consolidation across the two inherited estates, and managed services; leverage Printec's Eurobank Greece relationship as the reference.

signals.signal: Portal access mapped as at 01/08/2026. The quick/current-opportunities search (/epps/prepareCurrentOpportunities.do, /epps/quickSearchAction.do) is CAPTCHA-gated and was NOT bypassed. Two public routes are ungated and were used successfully: (a) /epps/common/viewOpenedTenders.do - a POST-searchable register of 18,187 opened tenders (fields: mode=search, title, uniqueId, contractAuthority, procedure), whose per-tender page /epps/eawarding/showDetailsOpenedTender.do?resourceId=N discloses BIDDER NAMES AND BID PRICES; and (b) /epps/cft/prepareViewCfTWS.do?resourceId=N - the full tender overview with estimated value, CPV, legal regime, duration and dates. The published 2026 annual-plan register (/epps/app/viewPublication.do, cycle 1000, created 31/01/2026, expiring 01/01/2027) holds only 14 organisation plans - Public Natural Gas, ETYFA, Nicosia district organisation, Public Works, University of Cyprus, Cyprus Institute of Neurology and Genetics, Asylum Service, Ministry of Education, Cyprus Agricultural Payments Organisation, Cyprus University of Technology and others - and contains NO central bank, NO Cyprus Post and NO bank plan. signals.source_name: eprocurement.gov.cy (e-PPS) - Δημοσιευμένο Ετήσιο Πλάνο Διαγωνισμών and Πληροφορίες Αποσφράγισης
signals.implies: Operationally important for Printec's bid desk: Cyprus discloses actual competitor bid prices per tender through the opened-tender register - rare in the region and directly usable for pricing intelligence (it is how the EAC counting-machine and Larnaca ATM bid prices in this file were obtained). Conversely the annual-plan route is near-useless in Cyprus, so forward pipeline must come from TED and entity websites.
signals.followup: Add /epps/common/viewOpenedTenders.do to the standing collection route for Cyprus competitor pricing; do not rely on the e-PPS annual plan; collect CBC from centralbank.cy + TED only.

coverage_notes: RESUMED FROM CHECKPOINT then extended. The prior partial file for this runDate held 6 CBC/Veridos signals; all were re-verified and kept, and the four gaps its 'remaining' note listed (Cyprus Post, commercial banks, open Cyprus TED notices, Deputy Ministry of Research/Innovation/Digital Policy and the e-PPS annual plan) were all closed this pass. Angles worked, in both English and Greek: (1) TED search API by place-of-performance CYP for 01/06/2026-01/08/2026 - 377 notices pulled over two pages, filtered on 44 CPV prefixes plus 20 EN/EL keywords, 59 candidates reviewed and 8 full notice PDFs downloaded and text-extracted locally with pdfminer.six; (2) eprocurement.gov.cy e-PPS - the CAPTCHA-free opened-tender register (18,187 records) swept with 27 Greek and English keywords (ATM, αυτόματων ταμειακών, αυτόματης ταμειακής μηχανής, καταμέτρησης, χαρτονομισμ, κερματ, μετρητών, χρηματοκιβ, θυρίδ, ανακύκλ, Glory, NCR, Diebold, POS, κάρτ, SIEM, SOC, HSM, self-service, κυβερνοασφ, ασφάλειας πληροφορ, ταυτότητ, βιομετρ, Ταχυδρομ, Τράπεζ, ψηφιακ, ταμειακ) plus contracting-authority searches for ΚΕΝΤΡΙΚΗ ΤΡΑΠΕΖΑ and ΚΕΔΙΠΕΣ, with per-tender bid-opening pages and CfT overview pages opened for the material hits; (3) the e-PPS published annual procurement plan register for 2026; (4) centralbank.cy tenders and announcements pages in Greek and English with a desktop UA; (5) Cyprus Post's own Προσφορές page; (6) Bank of Cyprus' own branch-model page; (7) Association of Cyprus Banks sector figures via CBN/InBusinessNews; (8) Cyprus Mail on the Eurobank-Hellenic merger; (9) KEDIPES tenders page via WordPress REST API and via a real browser. GENUINE GAPS: no Cypriot commercial bank publishes procurement notices anywhere public (they are private companies and are not on e-PPS or TED) - Bank of Cyprus and Eurobank Limited must be worked as direct-sales accounts, and that is itself the finding; the Central Bank of Cyprus 02/2026 SIEM outcome is genuinely undisclosed on every channel CBC uses; the JCC eID contract value is not published because both bid cycles were lodged off-system; and KEDIPES tender 14/2026 (NAC and switches, deadline extended to 22/07/2026) is known only from a search-engine snippet because its detail page now 404s, so it is logged as an access issue rather than as a cited signal.
access_issues: centralbank.cy returns 403 to the default fetch tool; resolved by re-requesting the same URLs with a desktop Chrome User-Agent via curl. eprocurement.gov.cy quick/advanced search (/epps/quickSearchAction.do, /epps/prepareCurrentOpportunities.do) is CAPTCHA-gated - NOT bypassed, since solving CAPTCHAs is out of bounds; worked around via the ungated /epps/common/viewOpenedTenders.do register and /epps/cft/prepareViewCfTWS.do overview pages, both of which required a real browser session (direct curl to /epps/cft/searchContractNotices.do returns HTTP 500 and /epps/announcements/listAnnouncements.do errors without a session cookie). kedipes.com.cy/en/tenders/ renders its list client-side and returned an empty body both to curl and in-browser; the WordPress REST API (wp/v2/pages/1697, wp/v2/posts, wp/v2/search) returns the page with empty content, and https://kedipes.com.cy/en/tenders/tender-no-14-2026/ and /tender-proc-no-13-2026/ now return 404 although both are still search-engine indexed. cypruspost.post/en/tenders 404s; the Greek path /el/prosfores serves the list but it stops at 2024.
